valuation._note: The bridge from earnings scenarios to DECISIONS. Return_s = (exit_multiple_s x fy26e_npat_s) / market_cap_now - 1 + cash_yield. Working in market-cap space avoids share-count drift (the HPG/TCX stock-dividend trap). exit_multiple is the single biggest judgment call in this file: it is where 'what is it worth' lives. probs are Layer-2 beliefs; confidence is the evidence-quality shrink applied to expected return (see decide.py).
valuation._npat_ttm_method: DERIVED FROM THE EARNINGS PATH, not from a guessed share count: npat_ttm = H1_26 + H2_25, where H1_25 = H1_26/(1+yoy) and H2_25 ~ H1_25 x 1.05 seasonality. This keeps npat_ttm internally consistent with the same H1 actuals the scenarios are built on. An earlier version derived it from estimated share counts and put MBB's TTM base ~35% too low, which made a normal bank look like a +85% expected return. Cross-check whenever prices refresh: pe_ttm x npat_ttm should land within ~5% of shares x price.

actuals._CREDIT_INPUTS_FAIL_VERIFICATION_2026_07: ESCALATION. The two credit fields in this block cannot both describe the same thing, and which one is right decides whether VPB's forward scenarios are comfortable or very hard. ARITHMETIC: credit_q2 1,060,000 against credit_start_fy 962,000 is +10.19%, NOT the +24.6% recorded in credit_growth_ytd. One of the two is on a different basis. WHAT THE PRESS ACTUALLY SAYS, and it is two different statements: (a) CONSOLIDATED credit reached ~1.06 quadrillion in Q1/26, +10.2% on end-2025 - which reproduces credit_start_fy 962,000 exactly; (b) PARENT-BANK credit reached ~1.06 quadrillion after SIX months, +24.6%. So the likely defect is that credit_q2 is the Q1 CONSOLIDATED figure while credit_growth_ytd is the H1 PARENT figure - a PERIOD error and an ENTITY error, checks 1 and 2 of charter section 3, sitting side by side in one actuals block as though they described one quarter of one entity. LOGICAL CROSS-CHECK: consolidated credit is by construction >= parent credit. If parent was ~1.06 quadrillion at H1, consolidated at H1 must EXCEED 1.06 quadrillion. So credit_q2 = 1,060,000 is too low for consolidated Q2 whichever reading is correct. WHY IT MATTERS: scenarios.credit_growth_fy is 30/35/40%. If H1 consolidated growth was +24.6%, the base branch needs only +8.3% more in H2 and is comfortable. If it was +10.2%, the base branch needs +22.5% in H2 - a step-change of the same character as the KDH handover finding. The company's own FY plan of +34% to 1.29 quadrillion consolidated is consistent with the 962,000 start, so the FY target basis IS consolidated. NOT RESOLVED and NOT GUESSED. The numbers are left exactly as they are; only the flag is added. The consolidated Q2 credit balance is readable directly from the Q2 statement. Confidence cut 0.85 -> 0.70 pending that read.

tcx._FTSE_IS_PHASED_2026_07_28: CONFIRMED by two independent searches: FTSE's Vietnam inclusion is implemented in MULTIPLE TRANCHES running from the 21-Sep-2026 effective date through to September 2027 - it is NOT a single event. UNCONFIRMED and single-sourced: the specific split of 10% Sep-26 / 20% Mar-27 / 35% Jun-27 / 35% Sep-27. A second search explicitly failed to corroborate those weights, so they are recorded as a claim, not a fact (charter section 3). WHY IT MATTERS EVEN WITHOUT THE EXACT WEIGHTS: ftse_event_tree prices 21-Sep as one discrete event with branches +20% (p=0.35) / +5% (p=0.45) / -15% (p=0.20), EV +6.25%. If September is the FIRST SLICE rather than the whole reclassification, those magnitudes describe something larger than what actually happens that day. THE FAIR COUNTER-ARGUMENT: passive money moves mechanically on effective dates, but markets front-run reclassifications, so price response need not be proportional to tranche size. Note though that much of the move may ALREADY have happened - the VN-Index jumped ~59 points on the April 2026 confirmation. The +20% branch is therefore a bet on a SECOND large move, on the first tranche, after the announcement has already been digested. RECOMMENDED, NOT APPLIED: re-weight the tree toward 'in-line, quiet digestion' and shrink the tail magnitudes. Changing probs is a judgment change reserved for a human (charter section 2), and doubly so here because the tranche weights are unconfirmed. Resolve from the LSEG/FTSE primary announcement.
tcx._EVENT_TREE_IS_NOT_WIRED_2026_07_28: STRUCTURAL, same family as the MBB/VCI finding. ftse_event_tree is read ONLY by run.py, which prints it into SNAPSHOT.md. decide.py never reads it. So the +6.25% expected value from the FTSE event does NOT reach expected returns, the ranking, or the optimizer's weights - it is narrative, not a driver, and a reader of SNAPSHOT.md would reasonably assume otherwise. This matters most for VCI, whose bull case is described in its own evidence string as 'an EVENT bet, not a franchise investment' - and the event is not in the numbers at all. Wiring it in, or labelling it clearly as narrative, is a machinery change and human-only (charter section 4).

MBB's base comes from nothing, so it cannot be stress-tested: if SBV changes MBB's quota or NIM compresses, there is no lever to pull. That is the real cost of the gap, and it is a reason to BUILD the model, not to distrust the number. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT TONIGHT. Building a driver block now from press summaries - one of which already mislabelled the period - then rebuilding it Thursday would waste the work and risk anchoring on the wrong numbers.
